text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.

-After one of the toughest winters ever, some people in the northern part of Norway want to move south. Tired of snow and ice, they read job ads in the newspaper in search of work in the southern parts of the country.
-The Centre Party, Christian People's Party and liberal Venstre have announced a joint platform for the election in September. The three parties form the middle-of-the-road opposition in parliament.
-While the Norwegian economy is growing quickly, the number of people who are deeply indebted stays at the same level.

-Norway Seafoods, a unit of Norwegian holding company Aker RGI, said a court in Chile had rejected its request for a licence to fish for blue whiting in Chile's fishing zone. The company will probably appeal against the ruling to the Supreme Court in Santiago.

-By investing 70 percent of the State Petroleum Fund in shares, the government would make it grow from 90 billion crowns to 485 billion crowns in 20 years, an analyst says. If the government keeps investing in bonds only, the fund is estimated to grow at half speed. The government has proposed to parliament to invest 30 to 50 percent of the oil wealth in stock markets.
-Norwegian brewery Mack's manager Haakon Bredrup says Mack, Borg, Carlsberg and Hansa are considering everything from cooperation to a merger of the breweries.
